annotations.chapterTitle: VII. Imperialism as a Special Stage of Capitalism

annotation.targetText:
By the critique of imperialism, in the broad sense of the term,
 we mean the attitude of the different classes of society
annotation.summary: Different social classes criticize imperialism for different reasons: ruling capitalists defend it, middle-class liberals want to reform it into peaceful commerce, and working-class revolutionaries aim to abolish it.
annotation.explanation: Different social classes criticize imperialism for different reasons: ruling capitalists defend it, middle-class liberals want to reform it into peaceful commerce, and working-class revolutionaries aim to abolish it.
annotation.context: Lenin distinguishes between middle-class nostalgia for 'free competition' and revolutionary Marxist analysis, which recognizes that imperialism cannot be undone without eliminating private property.

annotations.bookTitle: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism

annotation.targetText: From all that has been said in this book on the economic essence of imperialism, it follows that we must define it as capitalism in transition, or, more precisely, as moribund capitalism.
annotation.summary: Imperialism is decaying, moribund capitalism: the final transitional stage where corporate concentration and socialized production set the stage for a planned socialist economy.
annotation.explanation: Imperialism is decaying, moribund capitalism: the final transitional stage where corporate concentration and socialized production set the stage for a planned socialist economy.
annotation.context: Monopoly capitalism organizes production on a massive, global scale. All that remains is to transfer ownership of these socialized industries from private monopolists to society as a whole.

annotations.bookTitle: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
annotations.chapterTitle: X. The Place of Imperialism in History

annotation.targetText: The cleavage between "town and country," as well as the "development of this cleavage," formerly confined to one country only, are now being reproduced on a tremendously enlarged basis. Viewed from this standpoint, entire countries appear to-day as "towns," namely, the industrial countries, whereas entire agrarian territories appear to be "country."
annotation.summary: World capitalism reproduces the division between town and country on a global scale, turning industrial powers into 'towns' and agrarian colonies into 'country'.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin extends Marx's analysis of the urban-rural division of labor to the world economy, explaining how uneven capitalist development polarizes the globe into industrial manufacturing centers and dependent agricultural or extractive peripheries.

annotation.targetText: International connections may grow in scope, spreading over territories not yet drawn into the vortex of capitalist life. In that case we speak of the extensive growth of world economy. On the other hand, they may assume greater depth, become more frequent, forming, as it were, a thicker net-work. In that case we have an intensive growth of world economy.
annotation.summary: The world economy expands both extensively (through colonial annexation of non-capitalist lands) and intensively (through deeper global production ties).
annotation.explanation: Bukharin distinguishes the two dimensions of capitalist globalization: geographical expansion into precapitalist territories and the deepening interdependence of global industry, transport, and finance.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. II: Growth of World Economy

annotation.targetText: War in capitalist society is only one of the methods of capitalist competition, when the latter extends to the sphere of world economy. This is why war is an immanent law of a society producing goods under the pressure of the blind laws of a spontaneously developing world market, but it cannot be the law of a society that consciously regulates the process of production and distribution.
annotation.summary: Under capitalism, war is not an accidental breakdown of order, but an immanent law of capitalist competition extended to the world market.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin shows that eliminating free competition inside national borders does not end capitalist anarchy; instead, it projects competition onto the global arena as armed conflict between rival capitalist powers.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. III: Organisation Forms of World Economy

annotation.targetText: The conditions of direct exploitation and those of the realisation of surplus value are not identical. They are separated logically as well as by time and space. The first are only limited by the productive power of society, the last by the proportional relations of the various lines of production and by the consuming power of society.
annotation.summary: Quoting Marx's Capital Vol. 3, Bukharin explains how depressed working-class consumption forces monopolies to seek foreign sales markets.
annotation.explanation: Because capitalism restricts the purchasing power of the domestic working masses while expanding mass production, monopolies are driven to dump surplus commodities abroad and annex colonial markets.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. V: World Sales Markets and Changed Sales Conditions

annotation.targetText: We have in mind the disproportion between the development of industry and the development of agriculture as a source of raw material for the manufacturing industry.
annotation.summary: The lagging development of agriculture behind rapid industrial growth triggers a global scramble among monopolies to seize raw material sources.
annotation.explanation: Because monopoly ownership of land holds back agricultural output while manufacturing demand for cotton, rubber, timber, and ores skyrockets, imperialist powers fight to monopolize colonial raw material supplies.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VI: World Market for Raw Materials, and Change in the Conditions of Purchasing Materials

annotation.targetText: By concentration we understand the increase of capital that is due to the capitalisation of the surplus value produced by that capital; under centralisation we understand the joining together of various individual capital units which thus form a new larger unit.
annotation.summary: Concentration grows capital through reinvesting surplus value, while centralization merges existing capitals into giant trusts and state-capitalist blocs.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin applies Marx's laws of concentration and centralization to the world economy, showing how national economies coalesce into competing 'state-capitalist trusts' that wage war to centralize territory.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. X: Reproduction of the Process of Concentration and Centralisation on a World Scale

annotation.targetText: Yesterday, the main task of the moment was, as determinedly as possible, to nationalise, confiscate, beat down and crush the bourgeoisie, and put down sabotage. Today, only a blind man could fail to see that we have nationalised, confiscated, beaten down and put down more than we have had time to count. The difference between socialisation and simple confiscation is that confiscation can be carried out by “determination” alone, without the ability to calculate and distribute properly, whereas socialisation cannot be brought about without this ability.
annotation.summary: Confiscation requires only political determination, whereas genuine socialization requires the organizational capacity to calculate, account for, and distribute production.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes the ultra-left illusion that decreeing further nationalizations automatically creates socialism; real socialization demands nationwide accounting, administration, and disciplined economic coordination.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: It is not state capitalism that is at war with socialism, but the petty bourgeoisie plus private capitalism fighting together against both state capitalism and socialism. The petty bourgeoisie oppose every kind of state interference, accounting and control, whether it be state capitalist or state socialist. This is an absolutely unquestionable fact of reality, and the root of the economic mistake of the “Left Communists” is that they have failed to understand it.
annotation.summary: In a predominantly small-peasant economy, the primary internal threat to socialism is petty-bourgeois profiteering and resistance to state accounting, not state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: By attacking 'state capitalism' in 1918, the Left Communists inadvertently aided small-proprietor grain speculators and private black-marketeers who opposed all state regulation and accounting.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: Socialism is inconceivable without large-scale capitalist engineering based on the latest discoveries of modern science. It is inconceivable without planned state organisation, which keeps tens of millions of people to the strictest observance of a unified standard in production and distribution.
annotation.summary: Socialism requires the material foundation of modern large-scale engineering, scientific technology, and unified state economic planning.
annotation.explanation: Lenin emphasizes that socialism cannot be built on fragmented small-scale production; it requires assimilating the most advanced technological and organizational achievements developed under large-scale capitalism.

annotations.chapterTitle: IV. Large-Scale Engineering and National Accounting

annotation.targetText: State-monopoly capitalism is a complete material preparation for socialism, the threshold of socialism, a rung on the ladder of history between which and the rung called socialism there are no intermediate rungs
annotation.summary: State-monopoly capitalism socializing production on a massive scale forms the immediate material threshold to socialism once the working class holds state power.
annotation.explanation: Because monopoly capitalism centralizes banking, trusts, and distribution networks on a national scale, replacing the bourgeois state with a proletarian Soviet state turns state-monopoly mechanisms into instruments of socialist construction.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotations.chapterTitle: IV. Large-Scale Engineering and National Accounting

annotation.targetText: No. Only those are worthy of the name of Communists who understand that it is impossible to create or introduce socialism without learning from the organisers of the trusts. For socialism is not a figment of the imagination, but the assimilation and application by the proletarian vanguard, which has seized power, of what has been created by the trusts.
annotation.summary: Socialism is not an idealist figment of the imagination, but the working class's practical appropriation and mastery of large-scale organization created by capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Against the idealist fantasy that socialism can be invented out of pure revolutionary willpower without technical expertise, Lenin insists that the proletarian state must employ and learn from first-class technical specialists under workers' oversight.

annotation.targetText: There is no good practice without Marxist theory, that is clear. The greatest clarity of principle is necessary for us communists in this question. There must be a sharp distinction between ourselves and all other Parties.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary practice depends on theoretical clarity that separates communist women's liberation from bourgeois feminism and reformism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin stresses that communists must draw a clear class line between proletarian women's emancipation (which requires abolishing private property in the means of production) and bourgeois feminism.

annotation.targetText: They are, unfortunately, doubly sacrificed by bourgeois society. First, by its accursed property system, and, secondly, by its accursed moral hypocrisy.
annotation.summary: Capitalism forces impoverished women into prostitution through economic destitution and then hypocritically criminalizes them.
annotation.explanation: Following Rosa Luxemburg's materialist critique, Lenin notes that bourgeois society drives working-class women into prostitution through poverty while subjecting them to police persecution and moral condemnation.

annotation.targetText: Take them back to productive work, bring them into the social economy. That is what we must do.
annotation.summary: The socialist solution to prostitution is economic reintegration into dignified, productive social labor.
annotation.explanation: Consistent with Soviet policy later detailed by Alexandra Kollontai, Lenin argues that ending prostitution requires eliminating women's economic destitution and bringing women into collective production.

annotation.targetText: The great social question appears as an adjunct, a part, of sexual problems. The main thing becomes a subsidiary matter. That not only endangers clarity on that question itself, it muddles the thoughts, the class-consciousness of proletarian women generally.
annotation.summary: Treating class struggle as secondary to personal sexual theories confuses working-class consciousness.
annotation.explanation: Lenin warns that isolating sex and marriage from the struggle against capitalist exploitation inverts Marxist priorities and weakens revolutionary focus during acute political crises.

annotation.targetText: The decay, the corruption, the filth of bourgeois marriage, with its difficult divorce, its freedom for the man, its enslavement for the woman, the repulsive hypocrisy of sexual morality and relations fill the most active minded and best people with deep disgust.
annotation.summary: Bourgeois marriage traps women in legal and economic servitude while excusing male privilege and double standards.
annotation.explanation: Lenin condemns capitalist marriage laws that sanctify private property, restrict divorce, and enforce female subordination behind a facade of moral respectability.

annotation.targetText: The thesis must clearly point out that real freedom for women is possible only through communism. The inseparable connection between the social and human position of the woman, and private property in the means of production, must be strongly brought out. That will draw a clear and ineradicable line of distinction between our policy and feminism.
annotation.summary: True women's liberation requires abolishing private ownership of the means of production, distinguishing Marxism from bourgeois feminism.
annotation.explanation: While bourgeois feminism seeks equal rights within the existing capitalist hierarchy, Marxism proves that women's oppression is structurally rooted in private property and class exploitation.

annotation.targetText: We are establishing communal kitchens and public eating-houses, laundries and repairing shops, nurseries, kindergartens, children's homes, educational institutes of all kinds. In short, we are seriously carrying out the demand in our programme for the transference of the economic and educational functions of the separate household to society. That will mean freedom for the woman from the old household drudgery and dependence on man.
annotation.summary: Socializing housework and childcare through public kitchens, laundries, and nurseries liberates women from domestic servitude.
annotation.explanation: Legal equality on paper is insufficient if women remain chained to unpaid domestic labor; Soviet power builds collective public infrastructure so women can develop their full human and political capacities.

annotation.explanation: Historical shift in production: industrial capitalism stripped the domestic home of its self-contained manufacturing role, socialization of production into factories.

annotation.targetText: The family no longer produces; it only consumes. The housework that remains consists of cleaning, cooking, washing, and mending. These are difficult and exhausting tasks, but this work is different in one important way from the work our grandmothers did: these four tasks are of no value to the state and the national economy, for they do not create any new values or make any contribution to the prosperity of the country.
annotation.summary: Under industrial capitalism, domestic labor is reduced to non-productive, repetitive chores that absorb women's energy without creating recognized exchange-value, isolating women within individual households.
annotation.explanation: Under industrial capitalism, domestic labor is reduced to non-productive, repetitive chores that absorb women's energy without creating recognized exchange-value, isolating women within individual households.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: Instead of the working woman having to struggle with the cooking in the kitchen, communist society will organise public restaurants and communal kitchens.
annotation.summary: Socialization of domestic work: replacing private isolated kitchens and laundries with high-quality public dining halls, central laundries, and repair centers frees women from domestic servitude.
annotation.explanation: Socialization of domestic work: replacing private isolated kitchens and laundries with high-quality public dining halls, central laundries, and repair centers frees women from domestic servitude.

annotation.targetText: All this goes to show that responsibility for the child is passing from the family to the collective.
annotation.summary: Universal state responsibility: socialist society provides free creches, nurseries, school lunches, and healthcare, lifting the private economic burden of child-rearing from mothers.
annotation.explanation: Universal state responsibility: socialist society provides free creches, nurseries, school lunches, and healthcare, lifting the private economic burden of child-rearing from mothers.

annotations.chapterTitle: 3. The State Is Responsible for the Upbringing of Children

annotation.targetText: For the capitalists are well aware that the old type of family, where the woman is a slave and where the husband is responsible for the well-being of his wife and children, constitutes the best weapon to stifle the desire of the working class for freedom. The worker is weighed down by his family cares and is obliged to compromise with capital.
annotation.summary: How the isolated nuclear family serves capitalism: financial anxiety over feeding dependents forces workers to accept wage cuts and suppress revolutionary strikes out of immediate survival fears.
annotation.explanation: How the isolated nuclear family serves capitalism: financial anxiety over feeding dependents forces workers to accept wage cuts and suppress revolutionary strikes out of immediate survival fears.

annotations.chapterTitle: 3. The State Is Responsible for the Upbringing of Children

annotation.targetText: Marriage will lose all the elements of material calculation which cripple family life. Marriage will be a union of two persons who love and trust each other.
annotation.summary: Socialist marriage: removing financial dependence transforms marriage from a commercial property transaction into a genuine union based on mutual affection and equal comradeship, eliminating the economic roots of prostitution.
annotation.explanation: Socialist marriage: removing financial dependence transforms marriage from a commercial property transaction into a genuine union based on mutual affection and equal comradeship, eliminating the economic roots of prostitution.

annotations.chapterTitle: 3. The State Is Responsible for the Upbringing of Children

annotation.targetText: The bourgeoisie, historically, has played a most revolutionary part.
annotation.summary: Capitalism destroyed feudal ties and transformed production on a world scale, which is why Marx treats it as a progressive but temporary stage.
annotation.explanation: Far from being a simple denunciation of capitalism, the Manifesto praises its historical achievements: it swept away feudal, patriarchal relations and created productive forces larger than all previous generations combined. That same dynamism creates the conditions for its own overthrow.
annotation.context: This is the basis of the Marxist view that socialism grows out of the contradictions of developed capitalism rather than replacing a pre-capitalist society directly.

annotation.targetText: In so far as machinery dispenses with muscular power, it becomes a means of employing labourers of slight muscular strength, and those whose bodily development is incomplete, but whose limbs are all the more supple. The labour of women and children was, therefore, the first thing sought for by capitalists who used machinery. That mighty substitute for labour and labourers was forthwith changed into a means for increasing the number of wage-labourers by enrolling, under the direct sway of capital, every member of the workman's family, without distinction of age or sex.
annotation.summary: Subjugation of the whole working family: machinery enables capital to enroll women and child labourers under its direct sway.
annotation.explanation: By replacing physical muscular exertion with automated mechanisms, machinery allows capital to break craft barriers and employ women and children at depressed wage rates, devaluing adult male wages and subjecting the entire working-class household to factory exploitation.
annotation.context: Part IV, Chapter 15: Machinery and Modern Industry (Section 3: The Proximate Effects of Machinery on the Workman)

annotations.bookTitle: Capital: Volume 1 (The Process of Production of Capital)

annotation.targetText:
Whilst the cotton industry introduced child-slavery in England,
it gave in the United States a stimulus to the transformation of the earlier,
more or less patriarchal slavery, into a system of commercial exploitation.
In fact, the veiled slavery of the wage workers in Europe needed, for its
pedestal, slavery pure and simple in the new world.
annotation.summary: European industrial wage-labor stood on the pedestal of racial chattel slavery in the Americas.
annotation.explanation: Marx shows that British textile mills and industrial capitalism depended directly on cotton produced by enslaved Black labor in the American South, linking anti-racist abolitionism to the emancipation of wage workers.

annotations.bookTitle: Capital: Volume 1 (The Process of Production of Capital)

annotation.summary: A transitional post-revolutionary economy contains five intermingled socio-economic structures, from peasant small commodity production to state capitalism and socialism.
annotation.explanation: Rather than treating the transitional economy as an abstract binary between pure capitalism and pure socialism, Lenin conducts a concrete materialist analysis of the five coexisting modes of production in Soviet Russia.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: We must create a powerful international women's movement, on a clear theoretical basis
annotation.summary: Lenin insists that women's liberation requires an international mass movement grounded in scientific socialist theory.
annotation.explanation: Rather than leaving women's organization to bourgeois charities or spontaneous reformism, Lenin argues the Communist International must build a theoretically rigorous movement of working women.

annotation.targetText: There is no good practice without Marxist theory, that is clear. The greatest clarity of principle is necessary for us communists in this question. There must be a sharp distinction between ourselves and all other Parties.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary practice depends on theoretical clarity that separates communist women's liberation from bourgeois feminism and reformism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin stresses that communists must draw a clear class line between proletarian women's emancipation (which requires abolishing private property in the means of production) and bourgeois feminism.

annotation.targetText: In Petrograd, here in Moscow, in other towns and industrial centres the women workers acted splendidly during the revolution. Without them we should not have been victorious.
annotation.summary: Working-class women were indispensable to the victory and defense of the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution.
annotation.explanation: Lenin highlights that proletarian women in Russia bore extreme material deprivation and fought on the front lines of the revolution, proving their central role in working-class victory.

annotation.targetText: The first proletarian dictatorship is a real pioneer in establishing social equality for women. It is clearing away more prejudices than could volumes of feminist literature.
annotation.summary: Workers' power achieves concrete material and legal equality for women far beyond bourgeois feminist rhetoric.
annotation.explanation: By overthrowing capitalist property relations and placing working women in Soviet governance and public administration, the workers' state dismantled centuries of legal and social subordination.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: They are, unfortunately, doubly sacrificed by bourgeois society. First, by its accursed property system, and, secondly, by its accursed moral hypocrisy.
annotation.summary: Capitalism forces impoverished women into prostitution through economic destitution and then hypocritically criminalizes them.
annotation.explanation: Following Rosa Luxemburg's materialist critique, Lenin notes that bourgeois society drives working-class women into prostitution through poverty while subjecting them to police persecution and moral condemnation.

annotation.targetText: Take them back to productive work, bring them into the social economy. That is what we must do.
annotation.summary: The socialist solution to prostitution is economic reintegration into dignified, productive social labor.
annotation.explanation: Consistent with Soviet policy later detailed by Alexandra Kollontai, Lenin argues that ending prostitution requires eliminating women's economic destitution and bringing women into collective production.

annotation.targetText: The extension of Freudian hypotheses seems 'educated', even scientific, but it is ignorant, bungling. Freudian theory is the modern fashion.
annotation.summary: Lenin critiques bourgeois psychoanalytic fashions that replace materialist class analysis with individualist sexual speculation.
annotation.explanation: Lenin argues that fashionable Freudian pamphlets flourishing in bourgeois society divert working-class activists away from collective struggle into self-absorbed individual psychology.

annotation.targetText: Forms of marriage and of the family, in their historical development and dependence upon economic life, are calculated to destroy the superstition existing in the minds of working women concerning the eternal character of bourgeois society.
annotation.summary: Zetkin demonstrates that studying the historical evolution of the family exposes capitalism as a temporary, changeable system.
annotation.explanation: Drawing on Engels's Origin of the Family, Zetkin points out that when working women learn how family structures change across economic modes of production, they realize bourgeois property relations are not eternal.

annotation.targetText: The great social question appears as an adjunct, a part, of sexual problems. The main thing becomes a subsidiary matter. That not only endangers clarity on that question itself, it muddles the thoughts, the class-consciousness of proletarian women generally.
annotation.summary: Treating class struggle as secondary to personal sexual theories confuses working-class consciousness.
annotation.explanation: Lenin warns that isolating sex and marriage from the struggle against capitalist exploitation inverts Marxist priorities and weakens revolutionary focus during acute political crises.

annotation.targetText: The decay, the corruption, the filth of bourgeois marriage, with its difficult divorce, its freedom for the man, its enslavement for the woman, the repulsive hypocrisy of sexual morality and relations fill the most active minded and best people with deep disgust.
annotation.summary: Bourgeois marriage traps women in legal and economic servitude while excusing male privilege and double standards.
annotation.explanation: Lenin condemns capitalist marriage laws that sanctify private property, restrict divorce, and enforce female subordination behind a facade of moral respectability.

annotation.targetText: You must be aware of the famous theory that in communist society the satisfaction of sexual desires, of love, will be as simple and unimportant as drinking a glass of water. This glass of water theory has made our young people mad, quite mad.
annotation.summary: Critique of the "glass of water" theory: reducing love and relationships to mechanical biological urges is vulgar anti-Marxism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin rejects the popular distortion that communism reduces love to a trivial physiological need, noting that such mechanical reductionism ignores culture, mutual respect, and social responsibility.

annotation.targetText: Drinking water is, of course, an individual affair. But in love two lives are concerned, and a third, a new life, arises, it is that which gives it its social interest, which gives rise to a duty towards the community.
annotation.summary: Human love is fundamentally social rather than purely individual because it involves mutual lives and the community.
annotation.explanation: Unlike an isolated physical act, romantic and family relationships affect another person and potentially children, creating ethical and social responsibilities within a socialist collective.

annotation.targetText: Communism will not bring asceticism, but joy of life, power of life, and a satisfied love life will help to do that.
annotation.summary: Communist morality rejects religious asceticism and celebrates a healthy, fulfilled, and joyful human life.
annotation.explanation: Lenin clarifies that critiquing bourgeois promiscuity has nothing in common with monastic self-denial; socialism aims to free love from economic coercion so people can live full, joyful lives.

annotation.targetText: The thesis must clearly point out that real freedom for women is possible only through communism. The inseparable connection between the social and human position of the woman, and private property in the means of production, must be strongly brought out. That will draw a clear and ineradicable line of distinction between our policy and feminism.
annotation.summary: True women's liberation requires abolishing private ownership of the means of production, distinguishing Marxism from bourgeois feminism.
annotation.explanation: While bourgeois feminism seeks equal rights within the existing capitalist hierarchy, Marxism proves that women's oppression is structurally rooted in private property and class exploitation.

annotation.targetText: No special organisations for women. A woman communist is a member of the Party just as a man communist, with equal rights and duties. There can be no difference of opinion on that score. Nevertheless, we must not close our eyes to the fact that the Party must have bodies, working groups, commissions, committees, bureaus or whatever you like, whose particular duty it is to arouse the masses of women workers
annotation.summary: Equal membership in a single Communist Party combined with specialized Party women's commissions for mass agitation.
annotation.explanation: Lenin balances organizational unity (men and women fighting together in one vanguard party) with practical revolutionary reality (dedicated women's bureaus like the Soviet Zhenotdel to organize working women).

annotation.targetText: The rejection of the necessity for separate bodies for our work among the women masses is a conception allied to those of our highly principled and most radical friends of the Communist Labour Party. According to them there must be only one form of organisation, workers' unions. I know them. Many revolutionary but confused minds appeal to principle 'whenever ideas are lacking'.
annotation.summary: Lenin critiques the ultra-left Communist Labour Party for appealing to abstract 'pure principle' to reject practical organizational work among women.
annotation.explanation: Ultra-left sectarians in the German Communist Labour Party (KAPD) opposed dedicated Party women's commissions in the name of abstract organizational purity, ignoring the concrete material obstacles keeping working women from political life.

annotation.targetText: Unless millions of women are with us we cannot exercise the proletarian dictatorship, cannot construct on communist lines. We must find our way to them, we must study and try to find that way.
annotation.summary: Socialist construction and working-class state power are impossible without the active participation of millions of working women.
annotation.explanation: Lenin rebukes sectarian purists who oppose dedicated outreach to women, emphasizing that no mass revolutionary transformation can succeed without mobilizing half the working population.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

annotation.targetText: Our demands are practical conclusions which we have drawn from the burning needs, the shameful humiliation of women, in bourgeois society, defenceless and without rights.
annotation.summary: Communist immediate demands address the concrete daily exploitation and humiliation suffered by working women under capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Fighting for maternity protection, equal pay, and legal rights demonstrates in practice that the Communist Party champions working women against landlords, employers, and patriarchal laws.

annotation.targetText: Unfortunately it is still true to say of many of our comrades, 'scratch a communist and find a philistine'. 0f course, you must scratch the sensitive spot, their mentality as regards women. Could there be a more damning proof of this than the calm acquiescence of men who see how women grow worn out In petty, monotonous household work, their strength and time dissipated and wasted, their minds growing narrow and stale, their hearts beating slowly, their will weakened!
annotation.summary: "Scratch a communist and find a philistine": Lenin condemns male comrades who tolerate women's domestic drudgery at home.
annotation.explanation: Lenin exposes how patriarchal habits persist even among professed revolutionaries who treat women's political organization as secondary and refuse to share domestic burdens.

annotation.targetText: Our communist work among the women, our political work, embraces a great deal of educational work among men. We must root out the old 'master' idea to its last and smallest root, in the Party and among the masses.
annotation.summary: Women's emancipation requires systematic ideological struggle to uproot patriarchal "master" privilege among working-class men.
annotation.explanation: Lenin insists that communist work on the woman question is never just "women's work": the Party must actively re-educate male workers to abandon domestic privilege and treat women as equal comrades.

annotation.targetText: We are establishing communal kitchens and public eating-houses, laundries and repairing shops, nurseries, kindergartens, children's homes, educational institutes of all kinds. In short, we are seriously carrying out the demand in our programme for the transference of the economic and educational functions of the separate household to society. That will mean freedom for the woman from the old household drudgery and dependence on man.
annotation.summary: Socializing housework and childcare through public kitchens, laundries, and nurseries liberates women from domestic servitude.
annotation.explanation: Legal equality on paper is insufficient if women remain chained to unpaid domestic labor; Soviet power builds collective public infrastructure so women can develop their full human and political capacities.

annotation.targetText: For every day of the existence of the Soviet State proves more clearly that we cannot go forward without the women.
annotation.summary: The progress and survival of socialist society depend directly on the full participation and leadership of emancipated women.
annotation.explanation: Lenin concludes that building a new socialist order requires millions of working women actively shaping economic production, public administration, and cultural life.

annotation.targetText:
the determining factor in history
is, in the final instance, the production and reproduction of the immediate
essentials of li
annotation.summary: Human history is fundamentally shaped by two practical activities: producing physical goods to survive (food, tools, shelter) and producing new human beings (childbirth, family, and child-rearing).
annotation.explanation: Human history is fundamentally shaped by two practical activities: producing physical goods to survive (food, tools, shelter) and producing new human beings (childbirth, family, and child-rearing).
annotation.context: Engels lays down the bedrock principle of historical materialism. Social systems, moral codes, and legal structures do not fall from the sky; they are built upon how a society produces material goods and organizes family life.

annotation.targetText: the more the social order is found to be dominated by kinship groups

annotation.explanation: In early human history when technology and stored wealth were minimal, society was organized around tribal clan bloodlines rather than states or private wealth.

annotation.explanation: As private wealth grew, old communal tribal systems collapsed under class conflict. In their place, the state was created to protect private property and manage division between rich and poor.
annotation.context: This explains the historical transition from primitive communalism to class society. The state did not exist eternally; it arose specifically to enforce property rights and suppress class conflict.

annotation.targetText:
[Mother-right, matriarchate ; Ed.] In this
work the author advances the following propositions: 

(1) That originally man lived in a state of sexual
promiscuity, to describe which Bachofen uses the mistaken term
"hetaerism"; 

(2) that such promiscuity excludes any certainty of
paternity, and that descent could therefore be reckoned only in the female
line, according to mother-right, and that this was originally the case amongst
all the peoples of antiquity; 

(3) that since women, as mothers, were the only parents of
the younger generation that were known with certainty, they held a position of
such high respect and honor that it became the foundation, in Bachofen's
conception, of a regular rule of women (gynaecocracy); 

(4) that the transition to monogamy, where the woman belonged
to one man exclusively, involved a violation of a primitive religious law (that
is, actually a violation of the traditional right of the other men to this
woman), and that in order to expiate this violation or to purchase indulgence
for it the woman had to surrender herself for a limited period.
annotation.summary: 19th-century scholars falsely assumed that the modern patriarchal family had existed unchanged throughout human history, treating temporary capitalist marriage norms as eternal human nature.
annotation.explanation: 19th-century scholars falsely assumed that the modern patriarchal family had existed unchanged throughout human history, treating temporary capitalist marriage norms as eternal human nature.
annotation.context: Engels critiques bourgeois ideology for projecting modern capitalist family structures backward into prehistory. In reality, human family systems evolved dramatically across different economic stages.

we are compelled to adm

annotation.explanation: The consanguine (generation-based) family stage is no longer practiced anywhere today, but its historical existence is proven by ancient kinship naming systems preserved in language.
annotation.context: Engels shows how anthropologists deduce prehistoric social stages. Even after actual marriage customs change, old kinship terms linger in language, allowing historians to reconstruct earliest human family forms.

If the first advance in organization consisted in the exclusion
of parents and children from sexual intercourse with one another, the second
was the exclusion of sister and brothe
annotation.summary: Early human social organization evolved through successive taboos on inbreeding, first excluding parents and children, and then brothers and sisters from mating.
annotation.explanation: Early human social organization evolved through successive taboos on inbreeding, first excluding parents and children, and then brothers and sisters from mating.
annotation.context: Engels traces the biological and social drivers of early family structures. As communities prohibited marriage between close relatives, tribal groups organized into distinct clans (gentes) that required marrying outside the clan.

annotation.explanation: As men accumulated private property in livestock and land, they abolished traditional matriarchal inheritance customs so their wealth could pass directly to their biological children.
annotation.context: In early communal clan systems, descent was traced through the mother, and property stayed within the mother's clan line. Private property accumulation created economic pressure to shift to male-line father-right inheritance.

annotation.targetText:
The overthrow of mother-right was the world historical defeat of the female
sex. The man took command in the home also; the woman was degraded and reduced
to servitu
annotation.summary: The transition from matriarchal clan communalism to patriarchal private property was a devastating historical defeat for women, stripping them of social equality and confining them to domestic servitude.
annotation.explanation: The transition from matriarchal clan communalism to patriarchal private property was a devastating historical defeat for women, stripping them of social equality and confining them to domestic servitude.
annotation.context: Engels highlights this transformation as one of the most critical turning points in human history. Female subjugation was not a natural condition, but the direct result of private property accumulation and the rise of class society.

annotation.explanation: Monogamous marriage did not arise from romantic ideals, but as an economic system created so men could guarantee legitimate heirs to inherit their private wealth.
annotation.context: Engels analyzes the economic origins of patriarchal marriage. When individual men accumulated wealth (livestock, land, slaves), they demanded guaranteed paternity so their accumulated private property could pass directly to their biological offspring.

economic cond
annotation.summary: Monogamy was the first family structure driven primarily by property rights and economic inheritance rather than mutual affection or communal clan ties.
annotation.explanation: Monogamy was the first family structure driven primarily by property rights and economic inheritance rather than mutual affection or communal clan ties.
annotation.context: In early communal societies, resources and child-rearing were shared by the entire clan. Monogamous domestic units developed only after private property disrupted collective living.

can add: The first class
opposition that appears in history coincides with the development of

annotation.summary: The subjugation of women in patriarchal marriage was the earliest form of class oppression in human history, establishing the template for all subsequent economic exploitation.
annotation.explanation: The subjugation of women in patriarchal marriage was the earliest form of class oppression in human history, establishing the template for all subsequent economic exploitation.
annotation.context: Engels directly links gender oppression to class oppression. In early human history, women held respected positions in communal clans. The rise of private property restricted women to domestic isolation, transforming wives into dependent housekeepers.

annotation.summary: Historically, strict marital fidelity was enforced upon women to safeguard property inheritance, while male infidelity was socially tolerated or institutionally accommodated.

annotation.context: Engels highlights the structural double standard of traditional monogamous marriage systems, where women were legally bound to domestic chastity while men had legal or social access to concubinage and prostitution.

annotation.targetText:
The proof that the kinship organizations
designated by animal names in a tribe of American Indians are essentially
identical with the genea of the Greeks and the gentes of the Romans; that the
American is the original form and the Greek and Roman forms are later and
derivative; that the whole social organization of the primitive Greeks and
Romans into gens, phratry, and tribe finds its faithful parallel in that of the
American Indians; that the gens is an institution common to all barbarians
until their entry into civilization and even afterwards (so far as our sources
go up to the present) ; this proof has cleared up at one stroke the most
difficult questions in the most ancient periods of Greek and Roman history,
providing us at the same time with an unsuspected wealth of information about
the fundamental features of social constitution in primitive times ; 
before the introduction of the state.
annotation.summary: The clan (gens) was the universal social structure of human societies before the rise of private property, class distinctions, and state authority.
annotation.explanation: The clan (gens) was the universal social structure of human societies before the rise of private property, class distinctions, and state authority.
annotation.context: Engels highlights Morgan's discovery that early Greek, Roman, Germanic, and Native American societies were all organized around egalitarian kinship clans. These clans managed public affairs democratically without standing armies, police, or kings.

annotation.targetText: In economically backward and semi-colonial China the landlord class and the comprador class are wholly appendages of the international bourgeoisie, depending upon imperialism for their survival and growth.
annotation.summary: In semi-colonial countries, domestic landlords and comprador capitalists are direct appendages of foreign imperialism.
annotation.explanation: Mao defines the comprador bourgeoisie and feudal landlord class as structural extensions of foreign monopoly capital inside an oppressed nation. Unlike an independent industrial bourgeoisie, compradors act as commercial and financial middlemen extracting wealth from domestic workers and peasants on behalf of foreign imperialist powers.
annotation.context: Modern comprador elites in Latin America, Africa, and Asia manage local subsidiaries, export enclaves, and privatized utilities for Western multinationals while relying on foreign military aid to suppress domestic labor unions.

annotations.bookTitle: Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society

annotation.targetText: The middle bourgeoisie, by which is meant chiefly the national bourgeoisie, [3] is inconsistent in its attitude towards the Chinese revolution: they feel the need for revolution and favour the revolutionary movement against imperialism and the warlords when they are smarting under the blows of foreign capital and the oppression of the warlords, but they become suspicious of the revolution when they sense that, with the militant participation of the proletariat at home and the active support of the international proletariat abroad, the revolution is threatening the hope of their class to attain the status of a big bourgeoisie.
annotation.summary: The national bourgeoisie in semi-colonial nations is caught in a contradiction: it resents foreign imperialist domination but fears working-class militancy.
annotation.explanation: Mao formulates the classic Marxist analysis of the dual character of the national bourgeoisie in semi-colonial countries. Because foreign monopolies restrict their domestic market, national capitalists intermittently support anti-imperialist struggles; however, because they themselves exploit wage labor, they panic whenever working-class and peasant organization threatens private property, causing their right wing to defect to imperialism (as Chiang Kai-shek did in the 1927 Shanghai massacre).
annotation.context: Domestic manufacturing owners in developing countries often support state tariffs against foreign imports, yet quickly ally with right-wing coups or IMF austerity programs when domestic workers strike for higher wages.

annotations.bookTitle: Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society
annotations.chapterTitle: Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society

annotation.targetText: Though not very numerous, the industrial proletariat represents China's new productive forces, is the most progressive class in modern China and has become the leading force in the revolutionary movement.
annotation.summary: Despite its smaller size in an agrarian country, the industrial working class is the vanguard leader of the revolution due to its concentration in modern industry and total lack of private property.
annotation.explanation: Refuting mechanical determinists who argued that China's industrial working class was too small to lead a revolution, Mao explains why the proletariat exercises vanguard leadership: first, its high concentration in large-scale modern enterprises (railways, mines, shipping, and textiles), and second, its complete deprivation of means of production under triple oppression by imperialists, warlords, and capitalists.
annotation.context: During the 1922 to 1926 Hong Kong-Canton, railway, and Shanghai general strikes, China's two million industrial workers paralyzed foreign imperialist commerce and spearheaded the national liberation movement.

annotation.targetText: general principles laid down in the Manifesto are, on the whole, as correct today as ever
annotation.summary: Enduring validity of Marxist principles: foundational scientific analysis of class struggle remains intact.
annotation.explanation: Marx and Engels emphasize that while specific tactical demands vary with historical conditions, the core materialist analysis of class struggle, capital accumulation, and historical development remains universally valid.

annotation.targetText: The history of all hitherto existing society(2) is the history of class struggles.
annotation.summary: All recorded history is driven by struggle between oppressor and oppressed classes, not by great individuals or ideas.
annotation.explanation: This is the opening thesis of the Manifesto and the core of historical materialism: freeman and slave, lord and serf, guild-master and journeyman all stood in open or hidden conflict, and each epoch ended either in revolutionary reconstruction of society or in the common ruin of the contending classes.
annotation.context: Marx and Engels did not claim class struggle was a new discovery; they argued that it explains the transitions between modes of production and that capitalism simplifies society into two great camps.

annotation.targetText: What the bourgeoisie therefore produces, above all, are its own grave-diggers. Its fall and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable.
annotation.summary: By building large industry and a concentrated working class, capitalism creates the force that will overthrow it.
annotation.explanation: The proletariat is not an outside enemy of capitalism but its own product. Factory production gathers workers together, organises them and teaches them to act collectively, so the growth of capital is simultaneously the growth of its grave-diggers.
annotation.context: Later Marxists such as Lenin and Luxemburg used this passage to argue that organisation and political consciousness, not spontaneous misery alone, turn the working class into a revolutionary force.

annotation.targetText: Law, morality, religion, are to him so many bourgeois prejudices, behind which lurk in ambush just as many bourgeois interests.
annotation.summary: For the modern worker, law, morality and religion are not neutral truths but disguises for the interests of the ruling class.
annotation.explanation: Marx and Engels describe how wage labour strips the worker of illusions: daily experience shows that bourgeois law protects property, bourgeois morality excuses exploitation, and religion often sanctifies the existing order.
annotation.context: This is an early statement of the Marxist theory of ideology, which later became central to analyses of religion and the superstructure.

annotation.targetText: In place of the old bourgeois society, with its classes and class antagonisms, we shall have an association, in which the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all.
annotation.summary: Communist society replaces class antagonism with an association where each person's freedom depends on the freedom of everyone.
annotation.explanation: This sentence states the humanist goal of the whole programme. Abolishing private ownership of the means of production is not an end in itself but the precondition for individual development that is no longer bought at the expense of other classes.
annotation.context: It is frequently cited against the claim that Marxism seeks to submerge the individual in the collective.

annotation.targetText: The working men have no country. We cannot take from them what they have not got.
annotation.summary: Because workers hold no property in the nation, their interests cross borders and nationalism cannot unite them with their own employers.
annotation.explanation: The line answers the charge that communists want to abolish countries. Marx and Engels argue that the working class is already stripped of national character by capitalism and that its political supremacy must first be won inside each nation before it can become international.
annotation.context: The slogan underlies the internationalist position that Lenin later used against social chauvinism during the First World War.

annotation.targetText: But Communism abolishes eternal truths, it abolishes all religion, and all morality, instead of constituting them on a new basis; it therefore acts in contradiction to all past historical experience.
annotation.summary: The charge that communism destroys religion and morality is answered by pointing out that all past ideas were shaped by class antagonism.
annotation.explanation: Marx and Engels turn the accusation around: since all past society moved through class antagonisms, the ideas of every age share common forms. Communism breaks with traditional property relations and therefore with traditional ideas.
annotation.context: This is one of the clearest statements that Marxism treats morality and religion as historical products rather than timeless absolutes.

annotation.targetText: The proletarians have nothing to lose but their chains. They have a world to win.
annotation.summary: The closing call states that workers have no property interest in the present order and everything to gain from overturning it.
annotation.explanation: The ending contrasts the ruling classes trembling at a communist revolution with a working class that risks only its chains. It fuses the open declaration of aims with the demand for the forcible overthrow of existing social conditions.
annotation.context: Combined with the final slogan 'Working Men of All Countries, Unite!', it became the most reproduced line of the socialist movement.

annotation.targetText: In order that a man may be able to sell commodities other than labour-power, he must of course have the means of production, as raw material, implements, &c. No boots can be made without leather. He requires also the means of subsistence.
annotation.summary: The separation of producers from the means of production: workers are compelled to sell labour-power because they lack productive property.

annotation.targetText: For the conversion of his money into capital, therefore, the owner of money must meet in the market with the free labourer, free in the double sense, that as a free man he can dispose of his labour-power as his own commodity, and that on the other hand he has no other commodity for sale, is short of everything necessary for the realisation of his labour-power.
annotation.summary: The double freedom of the proletarian: free to sell labour-power, and free from any ownership of the means of production.
annotation.explanation: Marx underscores the historical irony of bourgeois "freedom". The proletarian is free in two senses: legally free as an individual to dispose of their labour-power on the market (unlike a feudal serf or slave), and simultaneously free (bereft) of any means of production or subsistence, forcing them to submit to wage labour to avoid starvation.
